question.problem:
An amusement park knows that $25%$ of its visitors ride the rollercoaster. The manager of the park conducts a random sample of $125$ visitors. Find a normal approximation for the probability that fewer than $40$ of them rode the rollercoaster. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Note: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

current_example.problem:
A popular streaming service has a database of $100$ million songs, of which $64$ million have a duration of less than $3$ minutes. If a user randomly creates a playlist with $128$ songs, find a normal approximation for the probability that between $64$ and $96$ (inclusive) songs in the sample have a duration of less than $3$ minutes. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size. *Hint: Two tables of values of $\Phi(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $\Phi(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\, 0.00 \,$$\, 0.01 \,$$\, 0.02 \,$
$\, -3.4 \,$ $\, 0.0003 \,$ $\, 0.0003 \,$ $\, 0.0003 \,$
$\, -3.3 \,$ $\, 0.0005 \,$ $\, 0.0005 \,$ $\, 0.0005 \,$
$\, -3.2 \,$ $\, 0.0007 \,$ $\, 0.0007 \,$ $\, 0.0006 \,$
$z$$\, 0.07 \,$$\, 0.08 \,$$\, 0.09 \,$
$\, 2.5 \,$ $\, 0.9949 \,$ $\, 0.9951 \,$ $\, 0.9952 \,$
$\, 2.6 \,$ $\, 0.9962 \,$ $\, 0.9963 \,$ $\, 0.9964 \,$
$\, 2.7 \,$ $\, 0.9972 \,$ $\, 0.9973 \,$ $\, 0.9974 \,$
current_example.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\widehat{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\widehat{\,p} \sim N\left( p, \dfrac{p(1-p)}{n} \right),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np > 5,$ and $n(1-p) > 5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n = 128,$ and

- the population proportion is $p = \dfrac{64\,000\,000}{100\,000\,000} = 0.64.$

Now, since

$$
np = 128(0.64) = 81.92 > 5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p) = 128(1-0.64) = 46.08 > 5,
$$

and the $n=128$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.64,\frac{0.64(1-0.64)}{128}) \\  & ∼N(0.64,0.0018).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the probability we wish to find. If between $64$ and $96$ of the songs in the playlist last less than $3$ minutes, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{64}{128}\le \overset{^}{\,p} & \le \frac{96}{128} \\ 0.5\le \overset{^}{\,p} & \le 0.75.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the probability we wish to find is
$P(0.5 \leq          \widehat{\,p} \leq          0.75).$
So, we convert $\widehat{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.5\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.75) & =P(\frac{0.5-0.64}{\sqrt{0.0018}}\le Z\le \frac{0.75-0.64}{\sqrt{0.0018}}) \\  & ≈P(-3.30\le Z\le 2.59) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.59)-P(Z\le -3.30) \\  & =Φ(2.59)-Φ(-3.30)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(2.59)=0.9952,\,Φ(-3.30)=0.0005.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.5\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.75) & =Φ(2.59)-Φ(-3.30) \\  & =0.9952-0.0005 \\  & =0.9947.\end{aligned}
$$
